g.text: Did you know? SQL was originally called SEQUEL before trademark issues shortened the name 🗄️
Did you know? A famous early computer bug was an actual moth found in a Harvard Mark II relay 🐛
Did you know? FORTRAN helped make high-level programming practical in 1957 🧮
Did you know? COBOL was designed so business programs could read more like English 📜
Did you know? C was created alongside Unix and still shapes modern systems programming ⚙️
Did you know? Git was created in 2005 to help manage Linux kernel development 🌿
Did you know? The word "debugging" existed before software but programmers made it iconic 🔧
Did you know? The first web browser was also an editor, so the web was born read-write 🌐
Did you know? The original World Wide Web ran on a NeXT computer with a note asking people not to power it off 💻
Did you know? Java was once called Oak before becoming Java ☕
Did you know? Python is named after Monty Python, not the snake 🎭
Did you know? JavaScript was created in about ten days 🕒
Did you know? TypeScript adds types but still compiles down to JavaScript 🧩
Did you know? C# was first released with the .NET platform in the early 2000s 💜
Did you know? The .NET name originally stood for Microsoft's vision of internet-connected software 🌐
Did you know? Blazor can run .NET code in the browser using WebAssembly 🧪
Did you know? REST is an architectural style, not a protocol 🏛️
Did you know? HTTP status code 418 says "I'm a teapot" 🫖
Did you know? DNS is often called the phonebook of the internet, but it behaves more like a distributed cache 📇
Did you know? A cache can make code faster and also make bugs harder to reproduce 🧊
Did you know? The fastest database query is the one you do not run 🚀
Did you know? Indexes speed up reads but can slow down writes 📚
Did you know? A missing database index can turn a simple lookup into a table-wide treasure hunt 🕵️
Did you know? SQL joins are where data relationships either shine or quietly explode 🔗
Did you know? NULL is not zero, not false, and not an empty string 🕳️
Did you know? In SQL, NULL usually means "unknown", which is why comparisons get weird ❓
Did you know? Time zones are one of software engineering's most reliable sources of pain 🕰️
Did you know? Leap seconds exist because Earth's rotation is not perfectly tidy 🌍
Did you know? Floating-point math can make 0.1 + 0.2 look suspicious 🧮
Did you know? Computers store many decimal fractions approximately, not exactly 🎯
Did you know? Naming things is jokingly called one of the hardest problems in computer science 🏷️
Did you know? Off-by-one errors are tiny mistakes with enormous confidence 😅
Did you know? The phrase "works on my machine" is a deployment strategy only in nightmares 🧯
Did you know? Rubber duck debugging works because explaining a bug forces your brain to slow down 🦆
Did you know? A race condition can disappear the moment you try to observe it 🏁
Did you know? Concurrency is not the same as parallelism 🧵
Did you know? A deadlock is two or more tasks politely waiting forever 🤝
Did you know? A mutex is basically a tiny bouncer for shared data 🚪
Did you know? Immutable data can make whole classes of bugs vanish 🧊
Did you know? Recursion is a function calling itself until it remembers to stop 🔁
Did you know? The base case is the exit sign in a recursive maze 🚪
Did you know? A stack overflow can happen when recursion forgets its manners 📚
Did you know? Big O notation describes growth, not exact speed 📈
Did you know? O(1) does not always mean fast, it means constant with input size ⚡
Did you know? Binary search is fast because it throws away half the problem every step ✂️
Did you know? Hash tables are fast until collisions show up at the party 🎲
Did you know? Sorting algorithms can be stable, which means equal items keep their order 🧷
Did you know? Quicksort is often fast in practice but has a scary worst case 🎢
Did you know? Merge sort needs extra space but keeps its promises nicely 📦
Did you know? The halting problem proves some questions about programs cannot be solved generally 🛑
Did you know? Turing machines are simple on paper and terrifyingly powerful in theory 🧠
Did you know? A compiler is a translator with very strong opinions 🗣️
Did you know? An interpreter runs code more like a live conversation 🎙️
Did you know? Just-in-time compilation waits until runtime to get clever ⚡
Did you know? Garbage collection saves you from some memory bugs and introduces timing surprises 🧹
Did you know? Memory leaks are not always dramatic, sometimes they just slowly eat the room 🪣
Did you know? A pointer is just an address, which is why it can be both powerful and chaotic 📍
Did you know? A null pointer is software's way of pointing at absolutely nothing 🕳️
Did you know? Buffer overflows became famous because programs trusted input too much 🧨
Did you know? Input validation is security wearing a boring hat 🛡️
Did you know? The best error messages tell you what happened and what to do next 🧭
Did you know? Logs are time machines for production bugs 🕰️
Did you know? A good trace ID can turn chaos into a breadcrumb trail 🍞
Did you know? Observability asks systems to explain themselves before they break 🔍
Did you know? Monitoring tells you something is wrong, observability helps you ask why 📡
Did you know? A health check that only says "OK" may be hiding an entire disaster 🚦
Did you know? Retries can fix flaky failures or accidentally amplify outages 🔁
Did you know? Circuit breakers in software borrow their name from electrical safety ⚡
Did you know? Idempotent operations can be retried without doubling the damage 🧯
Did you know? A distributed system is one where a computer you forgot existed can ruin your day 🌐
Did you know? Network calls are just function calls with weather conditions ⛈️
Did you know? Latency is why "just one more API call" is rarely just one more API call 🐢
Did you know? CAP theorem says distributed databases cannot have every nice property during partitions ⚖️
Did you know? Eventual consistency means the system is allowed to be temporarily awkward ⏳
Did you know? Message queues help systems breathe instead of shouting directly at each other 📬
Did you know? A queue can turn traffic spikes into orderly waiting lines 🎟️
Did you know? Backpressure is software saying "please slow down before I fall over" 🛑
Did you know? A cron job is just time-based optimism 🗓️
Did you know? Batch jobs usually fail at the least convenient hour 🌙
Did you know? The hardest part of scheduling is often the calendar, not the code 📅
Did you know? Caching invalidation is famously one of computing's hardest practical problems 🧽
Did you know? A stale cache can make yesterday look like today 🧊
Did you know? CDNs make the internet feel closer by copying content around the world 🌍
Did you know? Compression trades CPU work for fewer bytes on the wire 📦
Did you know? Gzip can make text shrink dramatically because text repeats itself a lot 🗜️
Did you know? JSON won the web partly because humans can read it without special tools 📄
Did you know? XML is verbose because it brought structure and self-description to data 🏗️
Did you know? YAML is friendly until indentation becomes a crime scene 📐
Did you know? CSV sounds simple until a comma appears inside a quoted value 🧾
Did you know? Regular expressions are tiny pattern machines disguised as punctuation 🧬
Did you know? A bad regex can accidentally become a denial-of-service machine 🧨
Did you know? Unicode lets software represent writing systems far beyond ASCII 🌍
Did you know? Emojis can be multiple code points pretending to be one character 🙂
Did you know? String length is surprisingly complicated once Unicode enters the room 🧵
Did you know? ASCII has 128 original characters, which is tiny by modern standards 🔤
Did you know? The newline can be LF, CRLF, or a tiny cross-platform headache ↩️
Did you know? Endianness is about which byte gets to stand first 🥄
Did you know? The phrase "little endian" comes from Gulliver's Travels 📖
Did you know? A bit can only be 0 or 1, but enough bits can cause a global incident 💡
Did you know? One byte is usually eight bits, but computing history has exceptions 🧱
Did you know? Base64 makes binary data look like text so systems can carry it safely 🧃
Did you know? Checksums catch accidental changes, but cryptographic hashes fight tampering 🔐
Did you know? A hash function should make tiny input changes look wildly different 🎲
Did you know? Passwords should be hashed, salted, and never stored as plain text 🧂
Did you know? Salting passwords helps defeat precomputed rainbow tables 🌈
Did you know? Encryption protects data by making it unreadable without the right key 🔑
Did you know? TLS is why the lock icon matters in your browser 🔒
Did you know? HTTPS is HTTP wrapped in encrypted transport armor 🛡️
Did you know? JWTs are signed, not automatically encrypted 🪪
Did you know? A JWT can be read by anyone who has it unless its contents are encrypted 👀
Did you know? Refresh tokens are powerful and should be treated like keys 🔑
Did you know? The principle of least privilege is security's version of "need to know" 🧷
Did you know? SQL injection works when data is accidentally treated like code 💉
Did you know? Parameterized queries are the seatbelts of database access 🪑
Did you know? Cross-site scripting happens when hostile scripts sneak into trusted pages 🕸️
Did you know? Authentication asks who you are, authorization asks what you can do 🪪
Did you know? A 401 says "please authenticate", while a 403 says "you still cannot enter" 🚪
Did you know? A 404 can mean missing, hidden, or "we are not telling you" 🕵️
Did you know? A 500 error is the server quietly admitting it had a bad moment 🧯
Did you know? Rate limiting is how APIs tell enthusiastic clients to take a breath 🌬️
Did you know? Pagination keeps APIs from dumping the whole warehouse at once 📦
Did you know? Cursor pagination is often safer than offset pagination for changing data 🧭
Did you know? API versioning exists because clients remember old promises 📌
Did you know? Backward compatibility is kindness for machines you have never met 🤝
Did you know? Semantic versioning turns version numbers into tiny contracts 🧾
Did you know? A breaking change can be one removed field away from chaos 💥
Did you know? Feature flags let teams ship code without turning it on yet 🚩
Did you know? Canary releases borrow their name from an old warning system 🐤
Did you know? Blue-green deployment swaps traffic between two production environments 🔵
Did you know? Rollbacks are easier when deployments are boring and repeatable 🔙
Did you know? CI is the robot that asks "does this still work?" after every change 🤖
Did you know? CD can mean continuous delivery or continuous deployment, and teams argue about it 🚚
Did you know? A flaky test is a trust problem wearing a test name 🎭
Did you know? Unit tests are fast because they keep the world small 🧪
Did you know? Integration tests prove your code can talk to its neighbors 🧩
Did you know? End-to-end tests are useful but can be slow drama queens 🎬
Did you know? Test data is often the secret villain of reliable testing 🧫
Did you know? Mocking too much can test your imagination instead of your software 🎭
Did you know? Code coverage can tell what ran, not whether the test was good 📊
Did you know? A passing test suite can still miss the bug users care about 🕳️
Did you know? Refactoring changes structure while preserving behavior 🧱
Did you know? Technical debt is not always bad, but the interest can be brutal 💳
Did you know? A small clean function can be more valuable than a clever one 🧼
Did you know? The best abstraction removes confusion, not just lines of code 🪄
Did you know? Premature abstraction can be as painful as duplication 🧩
Did you know? The DRY principle means avoid duplicated knowledge, not every repeated line 🌵
Did you know? SOLID is about design pressure, not magic architecture dust 🧱
Did you know? Dependency injection is a way to give code its tools from the outside 🧰
Did you know? Inversion of control means the framework calls you, not the other way around 🔄
Did you know? Clean architecture is mostly about keeping business rules away from noisy details 🏛️
Did you know? A monolith can be excellent if it is modular and well-kept 🏢
Did you know? Microservices turn local complexity into network complexity 🌉
Did you know? Splitting a bad monolith can create many tiny bad services 🧨
Did you know? The database is often the real integration point in enterprise systems 🧲
Did you know? Stored procedures can be brilliant or terrifying depending on discipline 🧾
Did you know? ORMs save time until you forget they generate SQL 🧠
Did you know? The N+1 query problem is a loop quietly ordering too many database trips 🚕
Did you know? Transactions give databases a way to say "all or nothing" 🤝
Did you know? ACID is not just chemistry, it is database reliability language 🧪
Did you know? Isolation levels decide how much weirdness concurrent transactions may see 👀
Did you know? Deadlocks can happen in databases too, not just threads 🔒
Did you know? Normalization reduces duplication, denormalization sometimes buys speed ⚖️
Did you know? A good schema is documentation that the database enforces 📐
Did you know? Migrations are database history written in executable form 🧾
Did you know? A backup you have never restored is mostly a hope file 🧯
Did you know? Disaster recovery plans matter most when everyone is tired 🌧️
Did you know? The cloud is just someone else's computers with APIs ☁️
Did you know? Containers package apps with their dependencies, not an entire magic universe 📦
Did you know? Docker images are layered, which is why build order matters 🧅
Did you know? Kubernetes is powerful because distributed systems need traffic control 🚦
Did you know? YAML errors have launched many debugging journeys in Kubernetes 🧭
Did you know? Infrastructure as code makes servers reviewable like application code 🏗️
Did you know? Environment variables are configuration until secrets accidentally leak 🚨
Did you know? Secrets belong in secret stores, not in commits 🔐
Did you know? Git remembers more than people expect, including secrets you thought you deleted 🕰️
Did you know? A Git commit is identified by a hash of its contents and history 🔗
Did you know? Git branches are lightweight pointers, not full copies of your project 🌿
Did you know? A rebase rewrites history, which is elegant until shared branches get involved ✍️
Did you know? Merge conflicts are Git asking humans to make a decision 🧑‍⚖️
Did you know? The commit message is a note to a future human, possibly future you 📝
Did you know? Good README files reduce support load before anyone opens an issue 📘
Did you know? Documentation goes stale unless it lives near the work 📎
Did you know? A diagram can explain a system faster than a thousand defensive comments 🗺️
Did you know? Comments should explain why, because code already shows what 🧠
Did you know? TODO comments are tiny promises with no due date ⏰
Did you know? Code review is partly bug hunting and partly knowledge transfer 🔍
Did you know? The best pull requests are small enough for reviewers to stay awake ☕
Did you know? Pair programming has one person driving and one person watching for cliffs 🧭
Did you know? Agile originally emphasized people and working software, not ceremony 📣
Did you know? Estimates are guesses wearing office clothes 👔
Did you know? The mythical man-month warns that adding people to a late project can make it later 📚
Did you know? Conway's Law says systems often mirror the teams that build them 🏢
Did you know? The fastest code is sometimes the code you delete ✂️
Did you know? A one-line fix can require three days of understanding 🧩
Did you know? Production bugs love assumptions more than they love code 🕵️
Did you know? The user's path through software is often different from the developer's mental path 🧭
Did you know? Accessibility improvements often make software better for everyone ♿
Did you know? Dark mode is easy until charts, contrast, and brand colors join the meeting 🌙
Did you know? Performance work starts with measurement because vibes are terrible profilers 📏
Did you know? The most reliable systems are usually boring in exactly the right places 🧱
